lines.text: Look at this lake. Calm. Blue. In one night, it breathed out.
lines.beat_before: hook: the crater lake at night, still, stars on the water

lines.text: Cameroon, August, nineteen eighty six. Villages sleep in the valleys below Lake Nyos.
lines.beat_before: the valley at night: huts, lamps in windows, crickets

lines.text: Late at night, people hear a deep rumble. Some see a white mist rise from the water.
lines.beat_before: the rumble; the lake surface lifts

lines.text: The mist is carbon dioxide, heavier than air. It pours over the rim and down the valleys, like water.
lines.beat_before: stinger in silence: the white plume rises

lines.text: By morning, the valleys are silent.
lines.beat_before: the mist reaches the village; a lamp goes out; the crickets stop; black

lines.text: One thousand, seven hundred and forty six people died that night. Many in their homes.
lines.beat_before: dawn: empty paths, doors open, cold ash

lines.text: For years, gas from deep below had gathered at the bottom of the lake, held down by the weight of the water.
That night, something disturbed it. Scientists still debate what.
Today, pipes draw the gas up from the bottom, so it cannot build up like that again.
lines.beat_before: stinger in silence: the deep layer lets go; then today, the degassing raft

lines.text: But other lakes on Earth are still holding their breath.
lines.beat_before: another lake at night, calm; one bubble
